title: UK public sector finances, October 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the first outturn whose reference month CONTAINS Budget day, still scored against the pre-Budget forecast
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/publicsectorfinancesukoctober2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the publisher's own release-calendar entry reads verbatim 'Public sector finances, UK: October 2026', '20 November 2026 at 7:00am', describing 'the headline measures of Public Sector Finance Statistics (net borrowing net cash requirement and net debt)', marked 'This release is not yet published.' The same page carries the Office for Statistics Regulation accreditation statement, so the designation is primary too and not inherited from a bulletin. Cadence independently corroborated from the ONS's own bulletin index (api.beta.ons.gov.uk search, fetched direct 2026-09-09): 137 consecutive PSF bulletins from 2015-04-23 to 2026-08-21 all fall on the 19th-26th of the month, and all 11 October-edition bulletins (2015-11-20, 2016-11-22, 2017-11-21, 2018-11-21, 2019-11-21, 2020-11-20, 2021-11-19, 2022-11-22, 2023-11-21, 2024-11-21, 2025-11-21) fall on 19-22 November. The gov.uk statutory pre-announcement register 404'd on the expected slug (2026-09-09) and is NOT claimed as a source. Filed estimate on the two counts this lane records for every ONS entry: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed research, from three sibling proposals
notes: PROPOSED THREE TIMES — by the uk-cpi-2026-11-18, uk-labour-market-2026-11-17 and uk-public-sector-finances-2026-10-21 lanes, all on 2026-09-09; ALL THREE READ IN FULL BEFORE THIS CANONICAL FILE WAS WRITTEN, AND THE PREMISE THEY SHARE IS REFUTED. Each framed the slot as the first borrowing outturn scored against the Budget-day (2026-10-28) OBR Economic and fiscal outlook rather than a superseded one. Two ONS primaries, both fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200), say the opposite, because the binding lag is EFO -> monthly profiles, not EFO -> publication. (1) Autumn Budget 2024-10-30: the bulletin published 2024-11-21 (D+22, the exact structural analogue of this print at D+23) states 'The statistics in this bulletin do not yet fully reflect these updated forecasts'; so does the 2024-12-20 one; the first to name the new basis is the bulletin published 2025-01-22 (D+84), verbatim 'This chart uses forecast data published in the OBR's Economic and fiscal outlook - October 2024 and monthly profiles published in December 2024.' (2) Autumn Budget 2025-11-26: the bulletin published 2025-12-19 (D+23, exactly this print's offset) states 'We expect corresponding monthly profiles to be published in January 2026' and, verbatim, 'New monthly receipts profiles consistent with the OBR's Autumn 2025 Budget will be used to inform our Public Sector Finances, UK January 2026 statistical bulletin on 20 February 2026' (D+86). D+84 and D+86; 2026-10-28 plus 85 days is 2027-01-21, which is the December-2026-data bulletin, roughly three prints after this one. So this release's 'versus forecast' line will still be scored against the 'Economic and fiscal outlook - March 2026 report' (named verbatim in the live 2026-08-21 bulletin, whose comparisons use 'corresponding monthly profiles published in April 2026'). WHAT THIS PRINT ACTUALLY IS, in that light: the first outturn whose REFERENCE MONTH contains Budget day (2026-10-28) while the profile it is measured against predates the Budget — measures in the numerator, pre-Budget profile in the denominator — and the first VAT month carrying the SI 2026/987 electricity zero-rate (in force 2026-10-01) as well as the first clean month after the Great British Summer Savings VAT reduction (25 July to 1 September 2026, ~GBP 300m, ONS bulletin 2026-08-21). MECHANICS the proposals also missed: they all noted that ONS splits CPI (2026-11-18, ONS primary) and PSF (2026-11-20) onto separate mornings, unlike the 2026-10-21 same-minute co-print, and concluded the morning is clean. The pre-dawn window is; the SESSION is not — 2026-11-20 is US monthly options expiration (opex-2026-11-20, medium, confirmed). Measured, that overlap is ordinary rather than notable: 42 of 137 PSF release days since 2015-04-23 (30.7%) fall on a monthly opex Friday, because PSF lands on the 19th-26th and the third Friday on the 15th-21st. Tiered LOW on a first-party null re-measured on double the sibling lane's sample: across 137 PSF release days since 2015-04-23, IGLT.L moved 1.07x an ordinary day (Welch t = 0.70), GBP/USD 0.92x, the US 10-year 0.89x, the S&P 500 0.95x, VIX 0.94x, and the FTSE 100 0.83x (t = -2.30, i.e. significantly QUIETER). Restricted to the 11 October-edition prints this one belongs to, IGLT.L runs 0.70x (t = -2.25) and has never closed beyond +/-0.63% on any of them. symbols: [], no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed, and this repo tracks no UK-listed name. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
